title: Monty Desai Exits as Canada Cricket Coach; Board Begins Search for Successor
excerpt: The Indian-origin coach departs after a brief tenure amid ongoing corruption investigations and ICC funding suspension.
body:
• Indian-origin coach Monty Desai has exited as head coach of the Canada men's cricket team after just a few months in the role
  • Cricket Canada's board has begun the search for a successor amid ongoing corruption investigations and ICC funding suspension
  • Desai's departure marks the latest in a long line of coaching upheavals — Canada has seen 16 coaching changes in 16 years
  • The ICC's Anti-Corruption Unit continues to investigate allegations surrounding Canada's T20 World Cup 2026 campaign

Monty Desai has exited as head coach of the Canada men's cricket team, with Cricket Canada's board confirming it has begun the search for a successor. The Indian-origin coach's departure comes barely months after his appointment in May 2026 and adds another chapter to the turbulent state of Canadian cricket governance.

A Brief Tenure Amid Deep Turmoil

Desai, whose full name is Mrugang Jagadish Desai, was appointed at what ESPNcricinfo described as "a tough time in the cricket set-up in the country." His hiring followed a sweeping administrative shake-up that included the court-ordered ouster of then-president Amjad Bajwa, the removal of board member Praim Persaud at a Special General Meeting, and the resignation of former secretary Maninder Gill.

Cricket Canada president Arvinder Khosa had framed Desai's appointment as a strategic reset. "Our foremost priority is to restore Cricket Canada's prominence through performance, professionalism, and a renewed and vitalized sense of purpose," Khosa said in May.

"Associate cricket is an important driver in the global growth of cricket today, and teams like Nepal and Afghanistan have demonstrated what belief, discipline, and fearlessness can unlock."

— Monty Desai, upon his appointment in May 2026

Corruption Scandal Looms Large

The backdrop to Desai's tenure has been a cascade of integrity concerns. Canada lost all four group-stage matches at the 2026 men's T20 World Cup — to Afghanistan, New Zealand, South Africa, and UAE — and matters deteriorated sharply when the ICC's Anti-Corruption Unit launched an investigation into allegations of corruption during the tournament, focusing on a match involving Canada.

A CBC investigative documentary titled "Corruption, Crime and Cricket" alleged that captain Dilpreet Bajwa's bowling during the match against New Zealand was under scrutiny. The 22-year-old Bajwa had been named captain just three weeks before the tournament, which was jointly hosted by India and Sri Lanka.

In May 2026, the ICC suspended funding to Cricket Canada for six months over governance-related concerns. The suspension dealt a significant financial blow — ICC distributions accounted for nearly 63 percent of Cricket Canada's total income in 2024, contributing CAD 3.6 million out of total revenues of CAD 5.7 million, according to ESPNcricinfo.

A Decorated Coaching Career

The 52-year-old Desai brought over two decades of international coaching experience to the role. Born in India, he built his reputation through stints with the Rajasthan Royals in the Indian Premier League, the Afghanistan national team, and the West Indies, where he served as batting coach from 2019 to 2022.

His most celebrated tenure was with Nepal from 2023 to 2024, where he helped the team regain ODI status, qualify for the 2023 Asia Cup, and reach the 2024 T20 World Cup — their second appearance in the tournament after a decade-long absence. He subsequently coached the Kathmandu Gurkhas in the Nepal Premier League before accepting the Canada position.

What's Next for Canadian Cricket

Desai's exit continues a pattern of coaching instability that has plagued Cricket Canada for decades. The organization has cycled through at least 16 coaching changes in 16 years, with the average tenure measured in months rather than years. The only period of sustained stability came during Pubudu Dassanayake's stint from 2007 to 2011.

With crucial ICC pathway competitions ahead and the funding suspension still in effect, Cricket Canada faces the challenge of attracting a credible successor while restoring institutional integrity. The board's search for a new head coach begins against the backdrop of ongoing anti-corruption investigations and what Cricbuzz described as "one of the most turbulent phases in Cricket Canada's recent history."
